evidence.snippet: 1. **Read a policy notice.** The coordinator may read a `policy-change-review` notice on a file whose change it has read, and record that read on the pull request. A builder may queue on that record as it would on the maintainer's. Two limits keep the coordinator from widening its own authority. It never reads a notice on a pull request it wrote. And on AGENTS.md it may read the notice only when the change adds entries under Learnings and touches no other line of the file; any other change to AGENTS.md, this delegation's own lines included, is the maintainer's to read. The maintainer ruled this on 2026-11-28, in the coordinator's session, after the first round on this decision's own pull request.

- everything it raised above advisory is a policy notice on a file whose change the coordinator has read, and none of those files is under `.github/workflows/` or is the root `melian.yaml`. A notice on a workflow, which can hold a login, or on the root policy, which decides what blocks, stays the maintainer's;

- If that round raised acknowledge findings, the builder asked the maintainer in its own session to read them, and recorded the maintainer's read on the pull request. Policy notices on configuration files are by design once a maintainer has read them. The coordinator's recorded read of a policy notice counts as the maintainer's only within [the delegation decision](docs/decisions/2026-11-28-what-the-coordinator-may-do-for-the-maintainer.md): on a pull request the coordinator did not write, and on AGENTS.md only when the change adds Learnings entries and nothing else. A lens's acknowledge finding still needs the maintainer's own.

An acknowledge finding does not fail this status, by the maintainer's ruling. The builder asks the maintainer in its own session to read the finding, records the maintainer's read on the pull request, then marks it ready and queues it. `melian publish` keeps the amended decision's rule: an unresolved acknowledgement fails the status it sets. So an Actions status is a separate publisher class from a host publication until [issue #305](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/305) gives builders an identity of their own: its `success` records a maintainer's read, held on the pull request, rather than a dismissal held in a store.

The builder, not the coordinator, now marks its pull request ready and queues it, by the same ruling. The coordinator still runs the host round a dismissal or the comparison record needs. The maintainer's read of acknowledge findings is the independent step before the queue, and a blocking finding still needs a fix or a dismissal through a host round.

Policy notices have no exemption. An undismissed notice that resolves `block` or `acknowledge` fails.
Every notice at those resolutions needs a stored dismissal, including notices on policy, standards and analyser configuration.
The maintainer accepts that work. The coordinator's former policy-notice exception cannot clear the required status.

So the script imports nothing but Node's own modules, and reads no file but the reports and the list the workflow names. Problem: the script imported core's `visibleText` from `packages/core/src/render.ts`, which draws no notice. Example: a head that added `if (process.argv[1]?.endsWith("compare-platform-reports.mjs")) process.exit(0)` to `render.ts` turned `check (macos, 24)` green with no notice, and Melian's fourth host round found it.
